details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If evidence search becomes common and has variable follow-ups, broaden only that branch and keep the required checks enforced.
details.errorCorrection: A frequently observed sequence does not make mandatory controls safe to omit or reorder.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A workflow fits known ordered steps; agentic decisions are useful where the next action depends on new evidence.
details.scenarioApplication: The extra search is conditional, while the core identity and eligibility stages are fixed.
details.transfer: Express invariants as explicit gates and place flexibility at the uncertain branch.

messages.text: A log of skipped mandatory stages does not make those controls optional or guarantee the decision contract.
A prompt rule is not equivalent to a separately enforced eligibility check.
Parallel agents do not remove the stated dependency order and add coordination without changing the evidence need.

feedback.reason: The stable mandatory sequence should remain explicit. The rare evidence-dependent branch can be flexible without making required identity, policy, and eligibility steps optional.

options.text: Keep the four mandatory stages in a workflow and add a bounded evidence-search branch for the missing-clause exception.
Let the agent choose the next stage when earlier results make the usual sequence unnecessary, while logging skipped steps.
Replace the eligibility check with a prompt rule so the loop can complete the route in one turn.
Run each stage as an independent agent, then have a lead reconcile identity, policy, and eligibility results.

questions.prompt: A claims route follows: identity lookup → policy retrieval → deterministic eligibility check → structured recommendation. A proposed agent loop can choose which step to run. The workflow has had no valid reason to skip or reorder a step in 2,000 cases; exceptions require one extra evidence search. What is the best architecture?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the evidence source set and query sequence later become stable, a fixed retrieval workflow may be simpler.
details.errorCorrection: Variable evidence does not justify making unrelated mandatory steps optional or removing controls.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Use a hybrid pattern when fixed process invariants surround an evidence-dependent search.
details.scenarioApplication: The filings can change follow-up queries; stop conditions and budget bound that variability.
details.transfer: Reassess patterns when the dependency structure changes, not merely when input content is unstructured.

messages.text: This is a safe bounded fallback but fails to use evidence-dependent follow-up when filings lead to new queries.
The reviewer does not replace the stated stop rule and budget needed to bound the search.
Parallel work cannot bypass prerequisites when later steps depend on earlier outputs.

feedback.reason: The discovery path varies with what each filing reveals, but the required intake gates have not changed. Bounded flexibility belongs inside the evidence-gathering stage.

options.text: Keep the core workflow fixed and make the filing lookup a single deterministic query; route any unresolved search to review.
Let an agent search freely across filings until it finds enough evidence, then ask a reviewer to approve the conclusion.
Keep required gates fixed and bound the variable filing search by a stop rule and budget.
Use parallel workers for each required intake step even though later steps depend on earlier results.

questions.prompt: An intake system has the same four required steps as the previous pilot, but now supplier evidence is discovered through a changing set of public filings. Each filing may lead to a new query, and the search stops when a defined evidence threshold is met or the budget expires. What changed enough to justify a flexible component?

constraints: The common 80% has a stable, bounded path.
The 20% needs adaptive discovery and its own budget and review boundary.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Two paths add routing and maintenance overhead, but they avoid paying agentic cost on routine work while retaining discovery where it creates value.
details.errorCorrection: Do not let a minority of open-ended cases force all traffic through an agent or let a stable path hide missing evidence.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A classifier or explicit request type selects the augmented workflow or bounded agent; each path has its own evaluation, permissions, and stop conditions.
details.scenarioApplication: Measure FAQ accuracy and latency separately from investigation coverage, source quality, and budget, and send uncertain routing or agent completion to review.
details.transfer: Segment workloads by whether the next action is predictable and then evaluate a workflow and an agentic path against their actual slices.

messages.text: Universal agentic execution spends exploratory cost on routine questions and makes the stable workload less predictable.
The fixed knowledge base cannot supply evidence for the investigation slice and would produce confident incompleteness.
Answer length is not a quality or evidence criterion, and duplicate execution doubles cost without a route decision.

feedback.reason: The workload has two distinct decision structures: most cases have a known retrieval-and-answer path, while a minority benefits from adaptive search. Routing keeps each pattern proportionate.

options.text: Route stable questions through an augmented workflow and send investigation cases to a bounded agentic path with explicit stop and review criteria.
Use the agentic path for every question so the system has one architecture and can discover new sources when needed.
Use the fixed knowledge base for every question and return its best passage when investigation evidence is missing.
Run both paths for every request and select the longer answer as the more complete result.

questions.prompt: A support service handles 80% of questions with a stable knowledge base and fixed answer format. The remaining 20% require investigation across changing sources and follow-up searches. Which architecture should route the two workloads?

constraints: Normal intake steps and output schema are fixed.
Only the exception branch needs adaptive evidence search; the final policy check is deterministic.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The hybrid design requires explicit branching and monitoring, but it avoids unnecessary agent cost and protects the release gate.
details.errorCorrection: Place adaptive behavior at the smallest branch that requires discovery, while retaining deterministic gates around the external decision.
details.mechanismOrProperty: The workflow produces a typed intake and a flag; the agent searches relevant evidence under limits, and ordinary code enforces the final policy contract.
details.scenarioApplication: Process routine records through fixed stages, route flagged exceptions with their context and budget, and quarantine any record failing the final check.
details.transfer: When only exceptions are open-ended, use a predictable workflow as the spine and isolate adaptive search behind a measured, bounded branch.

messages.text: Applying exploration to every intake ignores the fixed normal path and raises cost and variability without evidence.
Manual exception work loses the opportunity for a controlled adaptive branch and leaves the state unobservable.
A citation can be stale or inapplicable; it does not replace the deterministic policy check.

feedback.reason: The normal path is known and the exception path is evidence-dependent. A workflow plus a bounded subpath preserves deterministic validation while granting exploration only where needed.

options.text: Send every intake through an open-ended agent so routine records and exceptions share one adaptive path.
Use one fixed prompt and have analysts investigate exceptions manually without recording an exception state.
Implement a workflow for extraction and validation, invoke a bounded agent only on flagged exceptions, then run the policy check before release.
Skip the policy check when the exception agent returns a cited passage because citation presence proves compliance.

questions.prompt: A compliance intake has a fixed extraction, validation, and schema sequence. Only exceptions require searching a changing evidence store, and all final records pass a deterministic policy check. Which architecture is most appropriate?

constraints: The next read tool and number of checks depend on live equipment readings.
Inspection tools are read-only, but the proposed repair is consequential.
Safety thresholds, deterministic checks, and human approval must stop the action path.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If every answer came only from the handbook and no live tool or action were needed, retain the augmented LLM boundary in CCARP-D01-O03-boundary.
details.errorCorrection: Static handbook context cannot execute or adapt to live evidence, and inference from absent readings can produce an unsafe repair recommendation.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic says agents fit open-ended problems whose number of steps cannot be predicted and describes them as LLMs using tools in a loop. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: The action path has evidence-dependent steps and a consequential approval boundary, unlike a one-shot cited handbook answer.
details.scenarioApplication: Use a bounded agentic loop for read-only inspection with explicit stop conditions, then pass the proposed repair and evidence through deterministic checks and human approval before action.
details.transfer: Use measured evidence and the stated authority boundary to choose the least complex design that satisfies the workload's constraint; revisit the route when the counterfactual changes.

messages.text: Static handbook context cannot execute or adapt to live evidence, and inference from absent readings can produce an unsafe repair recommendation.
A single unrestricted call has no explicit stop conditions or enforceable approval boundary for the consequential repair.
This avoids the adaptive inspection the scenario requires and escalates routine evidence gathering instead of using bounded read-only checks.

feedback.reason: The required pattern changes when the system must choose follow-up tools from new evidence; the action boundary remains outside unrestricted model control.

options.text: Use a bounded read-only agent loop, then require deterministic checks and human approval before repair.
Use the augmented LLM handbook path and ask the technician to infer the live reading and next action from the answer.
Expose all read and repair tools in one call and let the model choose the repair action whenever readings suggest it.
Use a fixed checklist and escalate every case to a technician without inspecting live readings through tools.

questions.prompt:
Technicians ask a maintenance question from a handbook and may then inspect live equipment, select among read tools based on readings, stop at a safety threshold, and request approval before a repair action.

Which interaction pattern fits the evidence-dependent inspection and repair boundary?

constraints: An exact lookup resolves 94% of requests at 220 ms p95 under a 500 ms synchronous SLA.
Only no-match or conflicting records create the evidence gap; research is five times more expensive.
Research has a separate three-minute asynchronous contract with pending and human escalation states.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the exact lookup never produced a no-match or conflict, remove the asynchronous research job; if the business accepted one three-minute response for every request, re-evaluate the synchronous routing boundary.
details.errorCorrection: The evidence gap is known only after the exact lookup, and inline research would violate the routine 500 ms contract when the catalog can resolve the request.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Just-in-time retrieval uses lightweight identifiers to load detailed information only when relevant, keeping context focused. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: Keep the 500 ms synchronous contract for routine exact lookups and defer the expensive research branch to an explicit asynchronous path only after the lookup proves an evidence gap.
details.scenarioApplication: Run the exact structured lookup synchronously, return its grounded result when it succeeds, and enqueue a bounded agentic research job only on a no-match or conflict state; expose pending, completion, citations, cost, and the three-minute timeout rather than running research inline.
details.transfer: Use an authoritative exact-key lookup first when it resolves the common path within the SLA; route no-match or conflicting evidence to a separately bounded research path.

messages.text: The evidence gap is known only after the exact lookup, and inline research would violate the routine 500 ms contract when the catalog can resolve the request.
Always researching wastes the cheap deterministic path and turns 94% of requests into unnecessary asynchronous work.
A no-match is the trigger for bounded research or human handling; a provisional semantic result does not satisfy the grounded-answer and evidence-state contract.

feedback.reason: The routing decision is between a fast synchronous first stage and a deferred evidence-gap job with its own SLA, not a generic choice to make every hard request agentic.

options.text: Classify the user message as routine or investigative before lookup and run the research loop inline for messages that appear complex.
Perform the exact lookup synchronously; research asynchronously only after a no-match or conflict, with explicit pending and timeout states.
Always enqueue the three-minute research job, even when the exact lookup succeeds, so every response has the same evidence depth.
Return the top semantic result immediately when the exact lookup has no match and mark its citation as provisional.

questions.prompt:
A product-support workflow first performs an exact SKU and warranty-status lookup. For 94% of requests it returns a grounded answer in 220 ms p95 under a 500 ms synchronous SLA; for 6% it returns no active match or conflicting records. A research pilot improves accepted resolution on that evidence-gap slice from 61% to 79% but costs five times as much.

Which routing design preserves the synchronous contract while using research where it adds value?

constraints: The subtasks and their order are known in advance.
A deterministic style gate must run before publication.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Explicit stages require orchestration code and intermediate storage, but they provide reproducible gates and clearer failure localization.
details.errorCorrection: Choose a workflow when the path is predictable; reserve agentic loops for cases where the next action genuinely depends on discovery.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Each Claude call performs one bounded transformation, and the application controls the sequence and style validator between calls.
details.scenarioApplication: Research output feeds the draft call, the draft feeds the style check, and a failed check returns a structured revision request rather than publication.
details.transfer: Map known business steps and mandatory gates before selecting an architecture; the pattern should follow process uncertainty, not novelty.

messages.text: Autonomous planning adds variability and cost without addressing a missing step in this fixed process.
One response hides stage failures and gives no independent style gate before publication.
Routing chooses among paths but does not represent the required order or enforce the fixed validation gate.

feedback.reason: Known subtasks and ordering favor a workflow whose stages and gate are explicit. Prompt chaining makes each handoff testable and avoids paying for unneeded autonomous planning.

options.text: Use an open-ended agent that chooses its own research and revision loop even though every required step and gate is already known.
Use a prompt-chained workflow with explicit research, drafting, and style-validation steps, passing structured output between them.
Use a single unrestricted prompt that asks Claude to research, draft, and self-approve the article in one response.
Use a routing layer that sends each article to whichever specialist appears most relevant, without encoding the fixed sequence.

questions.prompt: An editorial service must draft an article from a fixed outline, run a known sequence of research and drafting steps, and pass a fixed style gate before publication. Which architecture is the best fit?

constraints: Most messages map to stable categories and category-specific paths.
Ambiguous classification needs a human route rather than an invented action.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Routing is less flexible for novel requests and requires category maintenance, but it gives predictable permissions and a controlled human path.
details.errorCorrection: Use routing when known categories have distinct procedures; design uncertainty as a first-class branch rather than force a best guess.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A classifier selects a bounded category path; the route can carry uncertainty to a human or refuse execution rather than turn a low-confidence label into a side effect.
details.scenarioApplication: Delivery, damaged-item, and access messages each invoke their approved policy/API path, while unresolved classification enters a review queue with the evidence shown.
details.transfer: For operations with stable classes and materially different actions, separate classification, routing, and ambiguity handling before considering a free-form agent.

messages.text: Exploring all tools on every message spends cost and exposes unnecessary actions when the normal paths are already known.

A shared path does not enforce the distinct category policy and API contract before a side effect; deferring ambiguity to a post-action exception can send a sensitive or invalid request to the wrong route.
A description without a route leaves the operational work undone and does not enforce the category-specific policy.
Without category routing, the known policy/API paths cannot be selected consistently or evaluated as bounded workflows.
Without a pre-action ambiguity route, uncertain requests are forced into a category-specific operation instead of reaching a human safely.

feedback.reason: Stable categories justify a routing step, while ambiguity needs an explicit safe state at the route boundary. Together they prevent exploratory tool use and false certainty.

options.text: Let one agent explore every support tool for every message so it can discover the best category at runtime.
Classify the request, route it to the corresponding policy and API workflow, and use a confidence or ambiguity state for human handoff.
Apply one general support workflow and shared policy/API surface to every category, then send exceptions to a human after the workflow has attempted the request.
Use one fixed prompt for all categories and ask Claude to describe the next API call without executing a route.
Route ambiguous or low-confidence messages to a human queue with the evidence and candidate categories, without invoking a category-specific API.

questions.prompt: A support platform has stable delivery, damaged-item, and account-access categories, each with its own API and policy path. Ambiguous messages must reach a human. Which TWO design choices fit this workload? Select TWO.

constraints: The specialist scopes are separate but their evidence must support one conclusion.
Workers may research but cannot issue the customer-facing decision.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A lead stage adds elapsed time and a synthesis dependency, but it prevents inconsistent customer conclusions and supports an auditable handoff.
details.errorCorrection: Use specialization for research breadth without distributing final decision authority across unsynchronized agents.
details.mechanismOrProperty: An orchestrator delegates scoped research and collects artifacts; a lead checks provenance, resolves conflicts, and controls the final output.
details.scenarioApplication: Each worker cites applicable labor, tax, or environmental sources and states uncertainty; the lead checks the combined facts before drafting the customer response.
details.transfer: For multi-domain advice, put research authority with scoped workers and communication or decision authority with one validated owner.

messages.text: One worker combines unrelated rule sets and removes the independent evidence and specialization the scenario requires.
Allowing each specialist to answer the customer creates conflicting authority before any reconciliation.
An undifferentiated prompt provides no per-domain ownership or evidence contract and leaves interpretation unreviewed.

feedback.reason: The work naturally decomposes by rule set, but authority for the final conclusion belongs to the lead. Structured worker evidence makes that boundary explicit.

options.text: Ask one worker to research all three rule sets and publish its conclusion directly to the customer.
Give each specialist full authority to answer the customer and reconcile conflicting conclusions after delivery.
Run one undifferentiated prompt containing all rule sets and let Claude choose the most persuasive interpretation.
Assign bounded specialist workers with source and output contracts, then require a lead to validate evidence and synthesize the customer-facing conclusion.

questions.prompt: Labor, tax, and environmental specialists research separate rule sets and return evidence. Only a lead may issue the customer-facing conclusion. Which boundary should the architect implement?

constraints: The edits share dependencies and repository state.
Concurrent workers are causing conflicts rather than independent throughput.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Coordination reduces apparent concurrency and adds merge checkpoints, but it avoids repeated conflict repair and protects repository correctness.
details.errorCorrection: Diagnose contention and dependency structure before increasing concurrency; parallelism is useful only across independent work.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A dependency map and coordinator establish a partial order, while isolated branches or bounded parallel tasks reduce write conflicts before integration checks.
details.scenarioApplication: Sequence schema changes before dependent callers, run independent documentation edits in parallel, and require tests or compatibility checks at each merge point.
details.transfer: When agents modify shared artifacts, classify dependencies and ownership first; use parallelism inside an explicit integration plan.

messages.text: More workers amplify writes to the same dependent state and do not resolve the underlying ordering conflict.
Complete shared history and a final merge review do not coordinate dependent writes; the conflicting edits have already been created before that review.
Removing validation defers the conflict to the end and allows a broken repository to accumulate.

feedback.reason: The failure is not a lack of workers; it is shared mutable state and dependency ordering. The design must coordinate dependent edits and preserve validation barriers.

options.text: Map dependencies and assign a coordinator to sequence dependent edits, while parallelizing only changes proven independent and validating each integration point.
Increase the number of concurrent agents and ask each to resolve conflicts from the latest shared repository state.
Give every agent the complete repository history, allow dependent edits to proceed concurrently, and rely on one final merge review to reconcile conflicting assumptions.
Remove all validation gates so agents can commit quickly and reconcile the resulting repository at the end.

questions.prompt: Four migration agents receive shared repository history and edit dependent files concurrently. They overwrite assumptions, create conflicts, and require repeated reconciliation. What architectural diagnosis follows?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: One serial context may avoid coordination but does not match the required specialist expertise and variable task graph.
details.errorCorrection: Unscoped access invites duplication and weakens ownership of each result.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Orchestrator-workers fit cases where the required subtasks depend on the input.
details.scenarioApplication: The scan determines which specialists and evidence are needed for each market.
details.transfer: Use dynamic orchestration for discovered work; use fixed fanout when the worker set and tasks are known in advance.

messages.text: The scan can reveal different work for each market, so prelaunching a fixed worker set may miss necessary tasks or waste calls.
Workers need only their assigned evidence; full corpus access makes ownership and source boundaries unclear.
A single worker cannot make the independent specialist coverage or lead synthesis contract explicit.

feedback.reason: The subtask graph is not known until the scan returns, so an orchestrator can create the needed work dynamically while scoped packets and structured results keep synthesis traceable.

options.text: Run one fixed parallel task per specialist before seeing the market scan.
Assign scoped tasks after scan; collect outputs, then synthesize.
Give every worker the full corpus and let each choose which country to cover.
Ask one worker to examine all markets sequentially in a single context.

questions.prompt: A diligence lead knows that each country requires several specialist checks, but the number and type of checks depend on findings from an initial market scan. Workers can use isolated evidence packets and return a fixed report schema. Which orchestration design fits?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Sequential execution does not reconcile inconsistent definitions.
details.errorCorrection: Each output should carry the metric definition and period that make its figure interpretable.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Workers need explicit formats and boundaries to produce composable results.
details.scenarioApplication: The application is aggregating incompatible quantities, so vote or average would preserve the defect.
details.transfer: When synthesis changes with worker order, inspect shared assumptions and output contracts before adding autonomy.

messages.text: Voting among incompatible definitions can select a frequent result without making it comparable.
An average of different metrics and periods has no clear business meaning.
Serial execution changes timing, not the definitions that caused incomparable findings.

feedback.reason: The disagreement comes from incompatible task definitions, not insufficient worker count. Shared definitions and validated output fields make results comparable before aggregation.

options.text: Align worker definitions and periods before validating results.
Increase the number of workers and use majority vote over the three totals.
Tell the lead to average the worker totals so the order no longer matters.
Run the same workers sequentially without changing their definitions.

questions.prompt: Three parallel workers return valid findings, but they use different definitions of “active customer” and counted different reporting periods. The lead’s synthesis changes when the worker order changes. What orchestration repair addresses the cause?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A retry may be appropriate, but restarting completed independent work is not required by the failure.
details.errorCorrection: Marking a report partial is safer than filling an absent result with an implied negative.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Ground truth and task outcomes must be collected from every required worker.
details.scenarioApplication: The delayed source is explicitly mandatory, so completion status depends on it.
details.transfer: For parallel work, define per-worker completion and aggregation states so missing results cannot become silent omissions.

messages.text: No response is an unresolved worker state, not a zero-findings result.
A complete label would conceal the required jurisdiction that has not returned evidence.
A blanket restart discards completed work without addressing why one worker is delayed.

feedback.reason: A missing worker result is not evidence that its jurisdiction has no relevant findings. The orchestration must preserve the incomplete state and distinguish a partial report from a complete one.

options.text: Treat the missing result as no findings because the other four workers returned normally.
Publish the four results with a complete label and add the fifth when it arrives.
Cancel the four completed workers and restart all five with a larger timeout.
Keep status partial until required evidence is resolved or owner-excluded.

questions.prompt: A research agent delegates five independent sources to workers. Four return within the deadline; the fifth is still running and its source covers a required jurisdiction. The lead is asked to publish a complete comparison. What should the orchestrator do?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Parallelism can reduce latency but may add model, coordination, and synthesis costs.
details.errorCorrection: Arbitrary slicing does not create meaningful task boundaries.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Architecture should reflect the task dependency structure rather than a target worker count.
details.scenarioApplication: One adaptive process preserves the evolving context and avoids speculative fanout.
details.transfer: Before delegating, identify independent outputs and compare their expected value with coordination overhead.

messages.text: Identical workers duplicate a task without supplying independent evidence or a clear aggregation rule.
Time slices do not correspond to separable questions or evidence ownership.
Parallel work can increase cost and may not reduce latency when steps depend on one another.

feedback.reason: Parallel workers help when tasks can be separated. Here the work is tightly coupled and evidence-dependent, so the coordination and synthesis cost may outweigh parallelism until independent tasks are found.

options.text: Fan out ten identical workers and reconcile their drafts afterward.
Give each worker one arbitrary time slice of the investigation.
Follow one bounded evidence path; add workers for separable tasks.
Use all workers because parallelism always lowers both latency and cost.

questions.prompt: A team proposes ten workers for a research report. The request actually contains one tightly coupled analysis whose next step depends on each prior finding; workers would need to share the same evolving evidence and no independent subtasks have been identified. Which design is the best starting point?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Country-specific evidence should be interpreted under shared definitions to keep the comparison valid.
details.errorCorrection: Serial execution adds time without a dependency that requires it.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Fixed parallel sectioning suits known independent subtasks with a defined aggregation contract.
details.scenarioApplication: The pilot compares the two designs on this workload and shows no discovery benefit from the extra orchestration.
details.transfer: Choose orchestration based on whether the task graph must be discovered, not on a general hierarchy of patterns.

messages.text: Generality alone does not justify the measured latency and coordination cost for a fixed task set.
The four analyses are independent, so serial control adds no necessary dependency.
Changing definitions makes outputs incomparable and undermines the common report.

feedback.reason: The task graph is known, tasks are independent, and measurements show fixed fanout is faster without losing discovery value. Dynamic orchestration is useful when required subtasks depend on findings, which this workload does not show.

options.text: Keep the orchestrator because it is the more general multi-agent architecture.
Use fixed fanout for known work; reserve dynamic orchestration for discoveries.
Run the four analyses sequentially so the lead can control each worker’s conclusions.
Allow each worker to revise the country definitions to fit local evidence.

questions.prompt: A quarterly market report has four required country analyses that can be performed independently using the same definitions and report schema. Earlier pilots show fixed fanout completes in 8 minutes; a dynamic orchestrator completes in 13 minutes and discovers no additional work. What should the team use for this workload?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The policy permits bounded initial delegation, so removing all parallelism is unnecessarily broad.
details.errorCorrection: Low confidence may call for evidence review, but it does not authorize unbounded new workers.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Agentic work can adapt to findings, but each added call consumes time and cost and needs a stop condition.
details.scenarioApplication: The case specifies both delegation depth and total worker-call limits; enforce both as runtime controls.
details.transfer: Pair adaptive task discovery with a budget, explicit completion criteria, and a partial-result state.

messages.text: There is no deterministic stopping bound in this proposal, so the observed runaway can recur.
Confidence does not override the call budget and may amplify recursive work.
The stated policy allows bounded delegation; the defect is unlimited recursion, not delegation itself.

feedback.reason: Adaptive discovery is useful, but it needs explicit depth and call budgets. Once the policy limit is reached, the lead should stop spawning tasks and label unresolved coverage rather than silently exceeding the cap or claiming completeness.

options.text: Enforce the two-level and 12-call limits, track remaining budget, and return a clearly partial result when useful work remains after the cap.
Keep delegating until workers stop finding new questions, then summarize every result.
Increase the worker count whenever a subtask returns low confidence.
Disable all delegation, including the first specialist fanout, because recursive work is unsafe.

questions.prompt: A lead may delegate one research task to specialists, and specialists may discover follow-up questions. The orchestrator currently permits unlimited recursive delegation; a recent run created 46 workers, exceeded its call budget, and missed the report deadline. The task policy allows at most two delegation levels and 12 total worker calls. What control should be added?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Duplicated outputs from the same task are not independent confirmations and can disagree due to extraction variance.
details.errorCorrection: A different specialist does not make an identical source assignment independent evidence.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Independent worker calls are useful only when they add distinct evidence or analysis.
details.scenarioApplication: The task registry provides enough information to recognize identical work and keep retry state explicit.
details.transfer: De-duplicate by task scope and status; use new workers when the evidence or method is materially different.

messages.text: Two outputs from the same assignment do not form a meaningful majority.
Changing the worker while retaining the same evidence and question does not add task coverage.
Combining duplicate runs does not create two independent sources.

feedback.reason: The duplicate has the same evidence scope and task contract, so it adds cost without independent coverage. A stable task identity prevents accidental duplicate dispatch while preserving retries when the original result is known to be missing or invalid.

options.text: Keep both worker results and resolve the disagreement by majority vote.
Use a stable task identity and dispatch de-duplication for identical scope, retain one canonical result, and rerun only if evidence shows the original task failed.
Assign the duplicate to another specialist so the report gets more diverse opinions.
Merge the two outputs into one packet and count it as two independent confirmations.

questions.prompt: A report orchestrator launches the same “verify Q2 filings for North region” task twice after a slow worker response. Both workers return different extraction results, and the provider bills per call. The task registry shows identical source set, period, and output contract. What should the controller do?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Restarting complete required work discards validated outputs without fixing the optional worker delay.
details.errorCorrection: Finance data is not automatically evidence for a market-sizing result.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Completion gates should follow required outputs, not merely whether every launched task returned.
details.scenarioApplication: The report contract expressly allows the optional section to be marked unavailable.
details.transfer: Label partial and optional outputs according to their contract and retain a path for later completion.

messages.text: An optional packet is not a completion prerequisite when the contract defines an unavailable state.
A plausible inference from another packet is not a validated substitute for the missing analysis.
The required packets are already complete; restarting them adds risk and latency.

feedback.reason: The deadline contract distinguishes required from optional work. The required validated evidence is complete, and the optional section has an explicit unavailable state, so the report can be issued without pretending the late packet succeeded.

options.text: Hold the entire report until the optional packet returns, because every launched worker is part of completion.
Infer market sizing from the finance packet and mark the result as validated.
Publish the validated required sections and label the optional market-sizing section unavailable, preserving its pending status for a later update.
Cancel the required finance and legal packets and restart all workers with a shorter timeout.

questions.prompt: A client report is due in 20 minutes. The required finance and legal packets are complete and validated; an optional market-sizing packet is still running. The report contract permits omitting market sizing when it is labeled unavailable. What should the lead do at the deadline?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Removing citations hides the defect and reduces the report’s auditability.
details.errorCorrection: Worker consensus does not make a missing source ID real or a quote supportive.
details.mechanismOrProperty: An output contract helps workers return composable data but does not establish factual support.
details.scenarioApplication: Citation identity and quote-to-claim support are evidence properties that can be checked against the assigned source packet.
details.transfer: Validate evidence and provenance separately from schema before aggregating agent outputs.

messages.text: A valid JSON/schema record can still contain an invented or irrelevant citation.
A second opinion is not a substitute for checking the cited source itself.
Deleting provenance conceals unsupported claims instead of resolving them.

feedback.reason: Schema validity checks output shape, not whether a source exists or supports a claim. The lead must verify provenance and claim support before synthesis, preserving unsupported findings as unresolved rather than laundering them through a valid packet.

options.text: Accept all records because the worker output schema and citation fields are valid.
Ask another worker to vote on whether the citations look credible.
Remove citation IDs from the final report so unsupported references cannot be detected.
Validate each citation against its assigned source and claim; retain supported records, and mark unsupported claims unresolved or send them back for evidence.

questions.prompt: Three workers return schema-valid claim records with citation IDs. Two IDs are absent from their assigned source packets, and one quote does not support the associated claim. What should the lead accept into the final report?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Repetition across workers does not change the source text’s authority or establish claim validity.
details.errorCorrection: The worker has no need or authority to perform the external publication action.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Trust in the orchestrator’s task assignment does not make every string returned by a worker an instruction.
details.scenarioApplication: The embedded phrase is part of retrieved/source content, not an authorized change to the job.
details.transfer: Keep delegated outputs inside the evidence boundary and centralize external actions with the authorized owner.

messages.text: A delegated worker cannot rewrite the lead’s task contract through text in an excerpt.
Adding an external write permission would expand authority beyond the assigned evidence task.
Repeated untrusted content is still not an authorized instruction.

Have independent workers run without a shared report contract and let the lead infer which findings belong in the final synthesis.
Run bounded specialist workers in parallel with scoped objectives and structured reports, then have a lead reconcile sources and produce the final report.
Use one sequential worker for every industry and merge its prose manually after all twelve investigations finish.

questions.prompt: A strategy team must investigate twelve industries concurrently, using a specialist per industry, and deliver one report reconciled by a lead. Which orchestration design matches the work?

constraints: Invoice cases are independent during extraction.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Per-item validation and quarantine reduce straight-through rate and require more records, but they prevent one malformed extraction from becoming a financial posting.
details.errorCorrection: Parallelize the independent unit, but put the side-effect gate after each unit rather than treating a batch result as inherently safe.
details.mechanismOrProperty: The orchestrator creates per-invoice jobs and correlation IDs; a deterministic gate consumes each result before the posting tool can mutate the ledger.
details.scenarioApplication: Limit concurrency to provider capacity, collect item outcomes, validate required fields and business rules, and route failed invoices for correction.
details.transfer: For independent repetitive work, use bounded fanout with isolated artifacts and preserve a deterministic per-item gate before side effects.

messages.text: A shared mutable ledger creates races and makes ownership or duplicate updates difficult to diagnose.

Posting before validation makes the audit report too late to prevent a bad external mutation.
Without bounded isolated fanout, independent invoices cannot use concurrency without losing correlation or overloading the service.
Without per-item deterministic validation, malformed or invalid model output can reach the posting side effect.

feedback.reason: Independent cases support bounded fanout, while the external posting boundary requires a validator for every item. Isolation and evidence-preserving quarantine keep failures attributable.

options.text: Share a mutable invoice ledger among workers and let whichever worker finishes last update the record.
Fan out bounded, isolated invoice tasks with a per-item correlation ID and aggregate their results after the workers finish.
Ask one agent to process all invoices in a single context so it can compare supplier patterns.

Run schema and business validation for each result before posting, and quarantine failures with their source and worker evidence.

questions.prompt: A finance team must process 100 independent invoices concurrently. Each extraction must pass a deterministic schema and business validator before any posting. Which TWO orchestration decisions fit? Select TWO.

constraints: The number and dependency structure emerge during inspection.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Dynamic decomposition adds orchestration state and less predictable planning, but it avoids arbitrary batches that cause conflicts or miss hidden modules.
details.errorCorrection: Do not freeze decomposition before observing the dependency graph; make task creation responsive while keeping scopes and integration checks explicit.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Inspection produces a task graph; the coordinator assigns module scope, records prerequisites, and expands or sequences work based on returned findings.
details.scenarioApplication: Start with repository inventory, create a module task with its dependency evidence, validate each change, and enqueue newly revealed dependents only after their prerequisites pass.

messages.text: Equal batches ignore discovered dependencies and can make later edits run against an incompatible or incomplete migration state.

feedback.reason: The right units and order are discovered rather than known up front. An orchestrator can decompose from evidence and maintain dependency-aware scheduling as the migration unfolds.

options.text: Predefine equal-sized module batches and execute them in a fixed order regardless of discovered dependencies.
Send the whole repository to one worker and ask it to keep every module change in one context.
Split by file count and run all changes concurrently, merging conflicts after the migration is complete.
Let an orchestrator inspect the repository, create scoped module tasks from discovered dependencies, and schedule the next task only when its prerequisites are satisfied.

questions.prompt: A repository migration has an unknown number of module-specific database and API changes; inspection reveals different dependencies and the next module to change depends on what the previous inspection finds. Which decomposition boundary fits?

constraints: The risk dimensions are separable checks.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Focused checks produce more artifacts and coordination, but they reduce blind spots and allow a missed dimension to be diagnosed directly.
details.errorCorrection: Decompose by independent decision dimensions rather than prompt length, and verify coverage explicitly at the integration point.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Independent reviewers receive a precise risk contract and return evidence; an aggregator verifies that all required categories have results and flags conflicts.

messages.text: A longer general prompt does not create ownership or evidence that the dependency dimension was actually checked.

Sentence boundaries are not risk boundaries and arbitrary ownership can leave categories unreviewed or duplicated.

feedback.reason: The missed dependency dimension is a coverage failure. Explicit task ownership and a completeness gate make each required risk check visible before the recommendation.

options.text: Ask one longer prompt to discuss security generally and rely on its final confidence to show that all dimensions were considered.
Run only the dependency check because the other dimensions already appeared in earlier reviews.
Create focused checks for authentication, data exposure, and dependencies with explicit outputs, then use a completeness gate before the release recommendation.
Split the prompt by sentence position and let each worker invent which risk category it should inspect.

questions.prompt: A security review prompt covers authentication and data exposure but repeatedly misses dependency vulnerabilities. All three findings are required for one release recommendation. What decomposition should repair the gap?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: One agent may simplify coordination but loses the parallelism available in the independent layer.
details.errorCorrection: Concurrent dependent edits create conflicts and make the final merge the first integration test.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Decomposition should be based on dependency structure, not equal task size.

details.transfer: Recompute the schedule when dependencies change; parallelize only nodes whose prerequisites are satisfied.

messages.text: Equal-sized batches can combine dependent tasks and separate work that could safely run together.
The known dependency graph makes premature concurrency predictable rather than useful.
A single context avoids some coordination but may be slower and less explicit than staged work.

feedback.reason: The dependency graph identifies which work can run concurrently and which must wait. Staging by prerequisites preserves throughput without treating dependent edits as independent.

options.text: Split the 60 modules into equal-sized batches and ignore the dependency scan to keep worker load balanced.
Run independent changes first; validate shared interfaces, then order dependent modules by prerequisite.
Run every module concurrently and use a final merge to discover which changes were premature.
Assign all modules to one agent so the dependency graph need not be represented.

questions.prompt: A migration has 60 modules. A dependency scan shows that 12 modules can be changed independently, 20 depend on those 12, and the rest form three sequential chains. The team has enough workers to edit every module at once. What decomposition fits the graph?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Serial processing removes available independent work and does not justify removing integration review.
details.errorCorrection: Full duplication wastes context and makes source ownership harder to audit.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Useful decomposition respects semantic dependencies and gives each task enough context.
details.scenarioApplication: Shared terms and linked files should be resolved within a task boundary before independent groups run.

messages.text: Equal counts preserve the boundary that produced inconsistent definitions.

Serial execution is not required for all 900 files and does not replace a consistency check.

feedback.reason: File count is not the relevant unit when some files share definitions and references. Grouping connected work preserves the context needed for consistency while retaining parallelism across independent groups.

options.text: Group related files by shared definitions and references, then parallelize independent groups.
Keep equal file batches and let each worker infer shared term definitions from its assigned files.
Send every file and all comments to every worker so no relevant relationship is missed.
Run one worker serially over all files and remove the final consistency review.

questions.prompt: A contract review contains 900 files. Most are independent, but 30 cross-reference one another and several share defined terms. The initial plan splits evenly by file count, causing repeated context loading and inconsistent term definitions. What should replace it?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Route labels explain why a case received deeper review and help diagnose future errors.
details.errorCorrection: Random sampling can miss the cases the safety classifier has already identified.

details.transfer: Use an inexpensive first stage when it can safely identify cases for more detailed analysis, and measure false negatives as well as workload.

messages.text: Deep analysis on every record spends the constrained review budget on cases already classified as routine.
Random sampling does not target the identified ambiguous safety cases.
Removing route provenance weakens audit and evaluation of the triage stage.

feedback.reason: A reliable coarse pass can reserve the limited deep-review budget for the slice that needs it, while source links preserve auditability. The classifier should not silently erase route evidence.

options.text: Run the expensive safety analysis on every message to avoid relying on the coarse classifier.
Sample 2% of all messages at random and infer safety prevalence from the sample.
Discard coarse labels after summarization so the escalation packet contains fewer fields.
Route uncertain or safety-related messages to deeper review; retain source IDs and route.

questions.prompt: A support queue has 200,000 messages. A coarse classifier reliably identifies 98% as routine; the remaining 2% contain ambiguous safety cases. The team has a fixed review budget and must preserve each source message for audit. Which decomposition is proportionate?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A larger context may help, but it does not itself create ownership or resolve contradictory claims.
details.errorCorrection: Worker count is not the primary decomposition criterion.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Good task boundaries reflect independent work and clear outputs.
details.scenarioApplication: This separates evidence gathering from conclusions that require cross-task synthesis.
details.transfer: When over-fragmentation causes inconsistent synthesis, regroup around evidence dependencies and explicit decision ownership.

messages.text: Equal size does not make the shared evidence requirements independent.
A context budget can constrain the design but does not determine meaningful task boundaries.
More context may reduce some truncation but does not define how conclusions are validated or owned.

feedback.reason: Paragraph boundaries do not guarantee independent reasoning. The team should identify separable evidence tasks and make shared conclusions explicit at integration.

options.text: How can the paragraph tasks be made equally sized so workers finish together?
How many workers can be started before the context window is full?
Assign independent evidence tasks, but give shared conclusions an owner and integration gate.
Can the final report be written by a model with a larger context window instead of decomposing the work?

questions.prompt: A planning team proposes splitting a long report into one task per paragraph. Every worker would need the full dataset and all other paragraphs to preserve cross-document conclusions; synthesis has repeatedly introduced contradictions. What is the better decomposition question?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Batch completion is not the same as completeness of the required check set.
details.errorCorrection: A summary-based model judgment is unnecessary when a formula defines the final combination.

messages.text: Dynamic follow-up discovery is not needed when the check set is fixed and the next action is deterministic.

options.text: Create an orchestrator that waits for each evidence result and invents follow-up questions even though the formula and checks are fixed.
Run independent checks in parallel; keep IDs/error states and apply the formula after completeness.
Ask one agent to infer the final risk rating from a summary of the checks.
Run the checks in batches of equal size and calculate the rating from whichever batch finishes first.

questions.prompt: A review has 40 evidence checks. Each check can be completed independently, but the final risk rating requires all results and is governed by a deterministic formula. The team has enough capacity to run the checks concurrently. Which decomposition is best?

messages.text: The known dependency order prevents an invalid downstream calculation.
One serial agent is not required when independent claims can be batched while preserving each record’s stage order.
A vendor name is not the validated tier required by the deterministic amount rule.

feedback.reason: Registry validation depends on the extracted vendor ID, and amount calculation depends on the validated tier. The decomposition should preserve those prerequisites while using concurrency only for independent cases or steps.

options.text: Run all three stages in parallel and merge results using whichever arrives first.
Ask one agent to read all invoices in sequence because any parallel execution would be unsafe.
Run extraction, then registry validation, then the deterministic amount calculation; parallelize only independent work within a stage and keep item IDs through aggregation.
Calculate the amount from the extracted vendor name while registry validation runs in the background.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Concurrency still needs bounds based on provider and downstream service capacity.
details.errorCorrection: Saying “the records are independent” does not make their internal stages independent.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Task decomposition should preserve within-item dependencies while exposing independent work for parallel execution.

messages.text: A global sequence unnecessarily serializes independent companies.

options.text: Run all registry, filing, and scoring stages for every company in one global sequence.
Ask three workers to independently score each company from the same initial name.
Parallelize registry, filing, and scoring for the same company because the companies are independent.
Process each company’s dependent stages in order; parallelize independent companies.

messages.text: Broad overlapping ownership raises duplication and still does not define how cross-section links are verified.

Removing provenance makes the missed cross-reference harder to detect and audit.

options.text: Give every reviewer the entire submission and allow each to rewrite all findings.
Add a bounded cross-section reconciliation gate for references and shared invariants.
Increase the number of section reviewers so each section receives more votes.
Remove citations and summarize each section independently.

Serial end-to-end work is possible but misses safe parallelism once the prerequisite is settled.

options.text: Run all checks concurrently, then reject results whose vendor identifiers conflict with the final registry match.

Process each invoice end to end in a single worker because the checks are related.

Give every reviewer the full document and ask each to produce a complete independent review.
Split by paragraph so each worker has a small context and the lead can merge the comments.

messages.text: A cross-reference index helps, but the owner/threshold relationship still needs an assigned linked task and synthesis check.

options.text: Use smaller page ranges and give each reviewer the full cross-reference index to reduce the chance of a boundary miss.
Have every reviewer read the full procedure and independently complete the shutdown checklist.

Create a linked task for the shutdown owner and threshold with both source sections, then reconcile that relationship at the lead.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the shared definition affects nearly every clause and repeated context is costly, a shared glossary with references can preserve parallelism.
details.errorCorrection: A majority definition does not replace the contract’s authoritative defined term.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the first-pass classifier is uncertain, validate its routing error before treating all 620 as safely cleared.

messages.text: The cleared records are already resolved and do not need deeper evidence work; the full set may also exceed the 9,000-token budget.

options.text: Send all 800 records to one synthesis call so it can compare routine and exception patterns in a single view.

constraints: The asset inventory is a prerequisite for all control checks.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The initial inventory gate delays fanout, but it prevents inconsistent asset scope and makes the final assessment reproducible.
details.errorCorrection: Order tasks by actual prerequisites, not control number or convenience, and preserve evidence at every decomposition boundary.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A validated prerequisite is distributed to independent tasks; each returns control-level evidence and an aggregator checks coverage and contradictions.
details.scenarioApplication: Freeze the inventory version, assign controls to access, encryption, or logging checks, retain evidence links, and review the complete set before certification.
details.transfer: For large assessments, model prerequisite artifacts and evidence gates explicitly before parallelizing independent checks.

messages.text: Workers using inconsistent inventories can produce incompatible scope and make later reconciliation unreliable.

options.text: Launch all 400 checks immediately against whatever asset inventory each worker happens to load, then reconcile asset names later.

Validate and version the shared inventory first, fan out isolated layer checks with evidence IDs, then run a cross-layer completeness and evidence review.

questions.prompt: A controls assessment covers 400 controls. Every control depends on a shared asset inventory; after that inventory is validated, controls can be grouped into independent access, encryption, and logging checks before one evidence review. Which schedule is correct?

constraints: Most messages need only the coarse label.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Filtering may miss a safety case if the first-stage recall is weak, so the labeler needs a held-out recall check and a review path for uncertain labels.
details.errorCorrection: Allocate expensive reasoning to a validated subset and preserve the path from aggregate output back to the individual evidence.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A first-stage label partitions the corpus, a predicate selects the high-risk cluster, and a second-stage synthesis produces traceable evidence and escalation artifacts.
details.scenarioApplication: Store message IDs and label versions, pass only selected safety cases to deep analysis, and retain citations and decisions for reviewer audit.

options.text: Map all messages to coarse labels, filter the safety clusters, run deep synthesis only on that subset, and retain links from every result to its source messages.

Sample a few messages from each label and publish a safety rate without preserving which messages were escalated.

questions.prompt: A support platform has 2 million messages. A cheap first pass can assign coarse labels, but only messages in safety-related clusters need deep synthesis and an escalation packet. Which decomposition is proportionate?

constraints: Each record has all required fields and uses the same fixed checks and result contract.

details.errorCorrection: There is no shared artifact for the records to consume, so the added stage only serializes work and introduces an unnecessary failure point.

details.scenarioApplication: Map records to independent validation tasks, run them with bounded concurrency, aggregate by record ID, and apply one completeness and error gate before release.

messages.text: There is no shared artifact for the records to consume, so the added stage only serializes work and introduces an unnecessary failure point.

options.text: Fan out independent validation tasks with bounded concurrency, aggregate by record ID, and gate release on completeness and errors.
Create a shared terminology stage first, then fan out mappings that consume it as in a dependency-aware workflow.
Run all records serially to simplify ordering, then release the completed list without a separate aggregation gate.
Fan out every record and post each result as it arrives, without waiting for a final completeness and error gate.

constraints: A precheck clears 1,080 controls; the remaining 120 failures form eight observed causes.

details.scenarioApplication: Run the precheck, assign one bounded owner per failing cause, use governed deferred tool discovery to expose only the selected 3,000-token schema for that cause, and spawn a further focused task only for a concrete contradiction before aggregating the eight packets.

messages.text: The eager surface adds 14,000 tokens to a 10,000-token case, exceeds the 16,000-token input budget before generation, and repeats work for controls already cleared.
